adversarialCheck.altExplanation1: Maybe this is a legitimate second real account for the same person (duplicate signup), not an anonymous-session artifact.
adversarialCheck.rejectedBecause: Every legitimate account-creation path in this codebase pairs the `users` insert with a second table: upsertPeOidcIdentity (peIdentity.ts) always also writes pe_user_identities in the same call; the email/password path (authCredentials.ts) always also writes user_auth_credentials; the admin POST /api/users route requires an explicit caller-supplied id+displayName+email. u_e274e3c3f5b7a9289c398edf has none of these three companion rows. The ONLY code path in this repo that inserts a bare `users` row with no companion table and defaults displayName to the id itself is `ensureUserProfile` (userProfiles.ts) called with a single argument from api-server's sessionMiddleware for the ephemeral anonymous-owner-cookie identity (middlewares/session.ts, attachEphemeralAnonymousOwner). The shape match (no email, displayName==id, no companion rows) plus the 25-second proximity to the real account's creation is consistent with: the operator's browser/webview had no verified PE session at the moment the Claude connector's WorkOS grant was bound, so an ephemeral anonymous owner id was minted and that id (not the real account) became the external_id/JWT sub WorkOS issued back (identity.ts's own comment names this path: 'WorkOS Standalone Connect: complete API user.id may appear as token sub').
adversarialCheck.altExplanation2: Maybe cortex-api and smartsite-mcp read/write different databases (a much simpler bug).
adversarialCheck.rejectedBecause: Both live Cloud Run services (gcloud run services describe, legacy-design-tools-prod project) resolve DATABASE_URL from the identical Secret Manager secret name DEPLOYMENT_DATABASE_URL_DIRECT in the identical project, i.e. the identical live database. Verified via JSON secretKeyRef inspection, not assumed.

boundaryHit: The code that decides WHICH user id gets passed to WorkOS as the external_id/subject at the moment the Claude connector authorizes lives outside this repo (grep for 'workos'/'WorkOS' across api-server and smartsite-mcp finds WorkOS referenced only as a hosted issuer/JWKS verifier -- no authorize-initiation code in this repo). That binding-time code is most likely in the hauska-map client (property-explorer app, not cloned in this worktree per dispatch scope) or in WorkOS's own hosted dashboard config. Per dispatch instruction, not reaching into a repo not owned from here.
conclusion: Architecture question, not a bug in this repo's read or write path. Matches dispatch Scenario A's disposition (stop, do not fake a connected state) via a different, now-evidenced mechanism than the dispatch's guess.
